output.summary: topological_sort crashes with KeyError for nodes that appear only as targets and does not maintain alphabetical ordering of ready nodes; shortest_path returns the path in reverse order. Both functions need adjustments to handle target‑only nodes, preserve input immutability, enforce alphabetical tie‑breaking, raise errors on cycles, and output the correct forward path.

requirements.description: topological_sort must treat nodes that appear only as targets (i.e., appear in adjacency lists but not as keys) as valid nodes with indegree count and no outgoing edges.
topological_sort must not raise KeyError for target‑only nodes; it must compute indegrees for all nodes present either as keys or as targets.
topological_sort must return a list containing every node from the graph (both keys and target‑only nodes) in a topological order that respects all directed edges.
When several nodes are ready to be placed next (indegree zero), topological_sort must select them in alphabetical order, ensuring deterministic ordering.
topological_sort must raise a ValueError if the input graph contains a cycle (i.e., no topological ordering exists).
topological_sort must return an empty list when given an empty graph {}.
topological_sort must not modify the input graph dictionary or any of its adjacency lists.
shortest_path must return the shortest (fewest‑edge) path from start to goal as a list of nodes ordered from start to goal, including both ends.
shortest_path must return [start] when start == goal.
shortest_path must return None when the goal node cannot be reached from the start node.
shortest_path must not modify the input graph or its adjacency lists.
shortest_path must correctly handle cases where start or goal appear only as targets (i.e., are not keys in the adjacency dict).
shortest_path must return the path in forward order (start → … → goal); the current implementation incorrectly returns the reversed order.
shortest_path must use breadth‑first search (or an equivalent algorithm) to guarantee the returned path is of minimal length in an unweighted graph.
